english.title: Intimidate witness in civil proceedings
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY..), which intimidated, and was intended to intimidate, another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), knowing or believing that

(A)_[he]_
(B)_[she]_

was or might have been a witness in proceedings set out in section 41 of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE PROCEEDINGS..), intending, by your act, to cause the course of justice to be obstructed, perverted or interfered with and the act was done after the commencement of the said proceedings
english.legislation: Contrary to section 39(1) and (4) of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) References to doing an act include references to issuing any threat (whether against a person or his finances or property or otherwise), or making any other statement.
(ii) See section 39(5) for clarification of "a witness".
(iii) See section 41 for the meaning of relevant proceedings. This offence DOES NOT cover proceedings for a criminal offence.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
